searchText: Could all clients ensure in their Windows builds that their build tools are including an application manifest with `<heapType>SegmentHeap</heapType>` in final exe because otherwise you'll get a terrible native allocator which; if it doesn't affect your runtime (for GC'd langs), will likely effect your db Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sbscs/application-manifests#heaptype Example PR in Nethermind: https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/7418/files Is Windows specific; but the effect we were seeing was db access speed degrading over time and profiling showing it was all in allocator contention (which completely resolved with this one weird trick)

excerpts.content:
Could all clients ensure in their Windows builds that their build tools are including an application manifest with  `<heapType>SegmentHeap</heapType>` in final exe because otherwise you'll get a terrible native allocator which; if it doesn't affect your runtime (for GC'd langs), will likely effect your db 

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sbscs/application-manifests#heaptype

Example PR in Nethermind: https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/7418/files

Is Windows specific; but the effect we were seeing was db access speed degrading over time and profiling showing it was all in allocator contention (which completely resolved with this one weird trick)
